slides.title: Jars for the Cold Store
slides.text: The second tower is the Cold Store, where Tally keeps samples on ice. A pot holds 3 liters of salt water, and each jar holds 1/2 of a liter. Before she pours, she wants to know how many jars to set out.

slides.title: Division asks how many fit
slides.text: You already know that 12 ÷ 4 asks how many 4s fit in 12. A fraction works the same way: 3 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 3. Each liter holds 2 halves, so 3 liters hold 6 halves. The answer is bigger than 3, because each piece is smaller than 1.

focus.cue: Each liter is the same as 2 halves.
Count the halves in 3 liters: 6 jars.

slides.title: A bigger pot, jars of 3/4
slides.text: A bigger pot holds 4 1/2 liters, and each jar holds 3/4 of a liter. Cut every liter into fourths, so both amounts are counted in the same piece. Then count how many groups of 3 fourths you can make.

visual.label: Six jars of three fourths fill four and a half liters

focus.cue: The pot holds four whole liters and one half.
Each jar takes 3/4 of a liter.

slides.title: Why you can flip and multiply
slides.text: Pour 1 liter into jars of 3/4 of a liter. It fills one jar and a third of the next: 4/3 jars. So every liter you pour counts as 4/3 jars, and dividing by 3/4 is the same as multiplying by 4/3. The fraction 4/3 is the reciprocal of 3/4.

slides.title: Check it by multiplying
slides.text: A quotient can always be checked. The pot of 4 1/2 liters filled 6 jars, so 6 jars of 3/4 must make 4 1/2 liters, and they do. The same check works for decimals: 2.4 ÷ 0.3 = 8, because 8 × 0.3 = 2.4.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for dividing with fractions.

words.means: the amount being shared out, such as the 3 liters in the pot
the size of one group, such as the 1/2 liter each jar holds
the answer to a division, such as 6 in 3 ÷ 1/2 = 6
a fraction turned over: the reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sub Zero at Pour and Count. Plan how many jars each pot will fill, then pour to test your plan. Six samples must reach the deep freeze.
slides.alt: Sub Zero on a phone: the lab screen shows a pot of 3 liters and one empty jar, with a stepper and a Pour button.
